issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee cannot enforce a mortgage decree by selling a new tenure right created for the mortgagor after the mortgaged proprietary interest has vested in the state.
material_facts: A simple mortgage secured a decree against the mortgagor’s proprietary interests in several villages.
While execution of the decree was pending, legislation vested the proprietary interests in the state.
The legislation created new tenure rights in certain lands for the former intermediary because of his cultivatory possession.
The mortgagee sought to sell those new tenure rights in execution of the mortgage decree.
issues.conclusion: The new tenure rights could not be sold in execution of the mortgage decree. For the lands that vested in the state, the mortgagee could pursue the compensation payable for the acquisition, rather than sell the new tenure rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6(a)(i) and 18 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, the proprietary interests in the relevant lands vested in the state, and the tenure rights subsequently conferred on the intermediary were new rights, not a continuation of the mortgaged rights. Section 6(h), read with section 73 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, directs the mortgagee to pursue the compensation for acquired mortgaged property; the new tenure rights are not compensation or substituted security. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.mortgage_decree_execution: A mortgagee is seeking to enforce a mortgage decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.mortgaged_proprietary_interest_vested_in: The proprietary interest that was mortgaged vested in the state.
predicates.new_tenure_right_created_after_vesting: After the vesting, the state conferred a new tenure right on the former holder because of that holder’s possession or cultivation of the land.
predicates.new_tenure_right_not_liable_to_mortgage_: The newly created tenure right cannot be sold to enforce the mortgage decree.

issues.definition: When execution of a mortgage decree concerns a mortgaged proprietary interest that vested in the state and a new tenure right was then created for the former holder, the new tenure right cannot be sold to enforce the decree.
